verses.1: A person who seeks to separate himself by flattery will find no peace, for in every case he will be despised.
verses.2: A fool does not desire understanding, but only to express his own mind.
verses.3: When a wicked person comes in with wickedness, so too does disgrace. With glory comes shame.
verses.4: The words of a person's mouth are deep waters, a spring of wisdom gushes forth.
verses.5: It is not good to favor a wicked person’s face, nor to turn aside a righteous person in judgment.
verses.6: The lips of a fool lead him into trouble, and his mouth calls for destruction.
verses.7: The mouth of a fool is his downfall, and his lips are a snare to his own soul.
verses.8: The words of slanderers are as thorns; they pierce the innermost parts.
verses.9: One who is lazy in his work is like one who causes destruction, a brother who brings ruin.
verses.10: The name of the LORD is a strong tower. The righteous run to it and are protected.
verses.11: The wealth of a rich man is his fortified city, and his riches are like a high wall.
verses.12: Before a fall, a man’s heart is lofty, but before honor comes humility.
verses.13: One who answers before listening is a fool and brings shame on himself.
verses.14: The spirit of a man sustains him in sickness, but who can bear a crushed spirit?
verses.15: A wise heart acquires knowledge, and the ears of the wise seek understanding.
verses.16: A gift opens the way for a person and brings him before the great.
verses.17: The righteous makes his own case in the first instance, but when the adversary comes, he examines him.
verses.18: A lottery ends disputes, and it divides even the closest of friends.
verses.19: An enemy is closer than a fortified city, and a dispute is more fierce than a strong gate.
verses.20: A man is filled from the fruit of his mouth; his belly is satisfied with the harvest of his lips.
verses.21: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
verses.22: One who finds a wife finds good, and receives favor from the LORD.
verses.23: The poor speaks pleas, and the rich answers with pride.
verses.24: There are friends who seek to exploit, but there is one who loves as a brother.

notes:
Notes
- v. 14: "a crushed spirit" is a literal rendering of "רוּחַ נְכֵאָה" — the Septuagint says "ὀλιγόψυχον δὲ ἄνδρα" ("a man of little spirit").
- v. 17: "the righteous makes his own case in the first instance" refers to the person who brings the claim first; the Septuagint renders it as "δίκαιος ἑαυτοῦ κατήγορος ἐν πρωτολογίᾳ" ("the righteous is his own accuser in the first instance"), which seems to invert the meaning and is likely secondary.
- v. 22: "finds a wife" is a direct rendering of "מָצָא אִשָּׁה" — the Septuagint reads "ὃς ἐκβάλλει γυναῖκα ἀγαθὴν", which diverges and appears to be an error or reworking.
